Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:10:1.hebrew: דקדשי בדק הבית היא - (ויש לה) דהא אינה קריבה למזבח, הלכך מותרת בגיזה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:10:1.english: That it is [an item] consecrated for Temple maintenance - (And it has [this status]), for it is not offered upon the altar; therefore, it is permitted to be shorn.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:10:2.hebrew: דלא שכיחא - ומילתא דלא שכיחא, לא גזרו רבנן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:10:2.english: As it is uncommon - And [regarding] a matter that is uncommon, the Sages did not issue a decree.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:11:1.english: Its price is expensive - And funds [equal to] its value are not so readily available to desacralize it upon them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:13:1.english: For a cleaver - For the purpose of the cleaver:

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:14:1.hebrew: לכתחלה - קאמר, והאי וכן אתולש קאי — דכי היכי דמותר לתלוש לצורך השחיטה (דהא פשיטא לך דרישא לכתחלה קאמר), הכי נמי לראות מקום המום? או דיעבד קאמר, והאי וכן אלא יזיזנו קאי, והכי קאמר: וכן מי שתלש את השער לראות את מקום המום, נמי לא יזיזנו ממקומו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:14:1.english: Ab initio - Does [the mishna] mean [that it is permitted] ab initio, and this [phrase] “and likewise” refers to “he plucks” — that just as it is permitted to pluck for the purpose of slaughter (for it is obvious to you that the first clause [of the mishna] is stated [as permitted] ab initio), so too [it is permitted to pluck] to see the place of the blemish? Or does [the mishna] mean [only] after the fact, and this [phrase] “and likewise” refers to “he may not move it,” and this is what it means: And likewise, one who plucked the hair to see the place of the blemish must also not move it from its place?

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:14:2.english: That is entangled in the ear - And there was a blemish on the ear.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:15:1.english: Where his slaughter proves concerning him - That he did not intend [it] for shearing.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:16:1.english: Rather, is it not [referring] to plucking - And it is saying [that it is permitted] ab initio.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:17:1.english: Deems permitted - The wool for benefit to the priest.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:1:1.english: [It is] permitted - Because the rationale is that [it is an act performed] without intention.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:2:1.hebrew: מסוכריא דנזייתא - ברזא של חבית, שכורכין סביבותיה נעורת ומטלניות כדי שתסתום הנקב יפה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:2:1.english: The stopper of a barrel - The plug of a barrel, around which they wrap tow and rags so that it will plug the hole well.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:2:2.hebrew: אסור להדוקיה - בתוך החבית בכח, משום סחיטה. ואע"ג דאינו מתכוין לשום סחיטה — אסור, אפי' לר"ש, דאמר במסכת שבת (דף מא:): דבר שאין מתכוין מותר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:2:2.english: It is prohibited to insert it tightly - Into the barrel with force, due to [the prohibition of] squeezing. And even though he does not intend any squeezing, [it is] prohibited, even according to Rabbi Shimon, who said in Tractate Shabbat (41b): An unintentional act is permitted.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:3:1.hebrew: ולא ימות - וכיון דמהדק לה, לא אפשר לה בלא סחיטה; אבל לפנות את השער, אפשר בלא תלישה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:3:1.english: And will it not die - And since he tightens it, it is impossible without squeezing; but to clear away the hair, it is possible without plucking.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:4:1.hebrew: הלכה כר' יהודה - אלמא ס"ל לרב, דבר שאין מתכוין אסור:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:4:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - Evidently, Rav holds that an unintentional act is prohibited.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:4:2.english: Without [the] men - Without Rav Ḥiyya and Rav Ḥanan.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:5:1.hebrew: ותולש לאו היינו גוזז - להכי אמר רב, הלכה כר' יוסי בבכור:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:5:1.english: And plucking is not shearing - For this [reason], Rav said: The halakhah is in accordance with Rabbi Yose regarding a firstborn.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:5:2.english: In an unusual manner - For it is not the usual way to pluck wool, but rather to shear [it].

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:6:1.english: One who plucks the wing - That he plucks a large feather from the wing of the bird.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:6:2.english: And one who snips it - After he plucked it, he cut off its tip.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:6:3.hebrew: והמורטו - שמחליקה מן הצדדין, ומורט מן הקנה השער:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:6:3.english: And one who strips it - In that he smoothes it from the sides, and plucks the hair from the quill.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:6:4.hebrew: גוזז ומחתך וממחק - מארבעים אבות מלאכות במסכת שבת (דף עג.). ממחק - מחליק:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:6:4.english: Shearing, cutting, and smoothing - [These are] among the forty primary categories of labor in Tractate Shabbat (daf 73a). "Smoothing" [means] making [it] smooth.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:6:5.hebrew: דהיינו אורחיה - שדרך נוצת עוף לתלוש, ולא לגזזה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:6:5.english: As that is its normal way - For it is the way with a bird's feathers to pluck [them], and not to shear them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:7:1.hebrew: מדרב ס"ל כדרבי יוסי - לגבי בכור, דתולש לאו היינו גוזז:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:7:1.english: From [the fact that] Rav holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei - With regard to a firstborn, that plucking is not [the same as] shearing:

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:7:2.english: Rabbi Yosei also holds in accordance with Rav - That an unintentional act is prohibited.

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:8:1.hebrew: ה"ג עיקרן מאדים וראשן משחיר - וכן בתוספ' דמס' פרה (פ"ב ה"ד):
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:8:1.english: This is the reading: Their roots are red and their tops are black - And so [it is] in the Tosefta of Tractate Parah (2:4).

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:8:2.hebrew: גוזז - את הראש שמשחיר במספרים, ומשייר מן המאדים ואילך, ואינו חושש משום גיזה בקדשים. אלמא, משום דאין מתכוין לשום גיזה אלא לתקן — שרי. שתי שערות שכולן שחורות פוסלות בפרה לגמרי, אבל עיקרן מאדים וראשן משחיר — אפשר בתקנה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:8:2.english: One shears - the top that is black with scissors, and leaves from the red [portion] onward; and he need not be concerned about [the prohibition of] shearing consecrated animals. Evidently, because he does not intend for the sake of shearing, but rather to rectify [the heifer], it is permitted. Two hairs that are entirely black disqualify the [red] heifer completely, but [if] their roots are red and their tops are black, rectification is possible:

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:9:1.hebrew: דלאו בת גיזה - שאין לפרות צמר, הלכך לא אסירא בגיזה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:9:1.english: That it is not subject to shearing - For cows do not have wool; therefore, it is not forbidden to shear [it].

Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:9:2.hebrew: לא תעבוד ולא תגוז - וי"ו מוסף על ענין ראשון, וילמדו שניהם זה מזה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 25a:9:2.english: You shall not work and you shall not shear - The [letter] vav adds onto the first matter, and both of them are learned from one another:

Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:17:1.hebrew: שער בכור בעל מום שנשר כו' - כולה הך שמעתא מוכחא דגיזת פסולי המוקדשין שרי מדאורייתא, ואפי' רבנן דאסרי — מפרש בגמ' גזירה: דלמא אתי לאשהויה. והא דדרשינן לעיל (בכורות דף ו:) "תזבח" ולא גיזה — היינו תזבח ולא תגוז. ותימה לרבי: דאמרי' בפרק שני דחולין (דף לו:) גבי "על הארץ תשפכנו כמים": ההוא למשרי דמן של פסולי המוקדשים הוא דאתא, דס״ד: הואיל ואסירי בגיזה ועבודה, דמן נמי ליבעי קבורה, קא משמע לן. והיכי תיסק אדעתין לאסור דמן [בהנאה] משום דאסירי בגיזה ועבודה? הא אפי' הגיזה עצמה מותרת! וכ״ת: הא דשריא מדאורייתא — היינו בנשר, אבל גוזז דמתכוין אסור? חדא: דמתכוין דדם כנשר גיזה. ועוד: אפילו בתולש פליגי, כדמוכח בסוף פירקין (בכורות דף כו.) דשרי (ר״ע), מכלל כי אסרי רבנן — מדרבנן. ואפי' בעולה תמימה לא מיתסרא הגיזה אלא מדרבנן, כדמוכח לקמן גבי תולש צמר מעולה תמימה; והא דפריך: "תולש מי איכא למאן דשרי?" — היינו מדרבנן, כדפי' שם בקונטרס משום דרשע הוא. ועוד קשה בההוא דחולין: למה לי קרא דם פסולי המוקדשין דשרי בהנאה? והלא אף בקדשים דם מותר בהנאה משנעשית מצותו, והתם דליכא מצוה למה יהא אסור? ועוד: מאי קאמר "הואיל ואסירי בגיזה ועבודה"? והא לאחר שחיטה מותר לגזוז ולעבוד, דמזביחה ואילך הכל מותר, והתם בדם שחיטה איירי! וחלב נמי לא אסרינן מדכתיב "בשר", (אלא) מחיים, ולא לאחר שחיטה — כמו למאן דדריש לעיל בפ' שני (בכורות דף טו:): "אין לך בהם היתר אכילה אלא משעת זביחה ואילך". ועוד: דשרי לכולי עלמא, מדבעי למילף היתר חלב בפרק קמא (לעיל בכורות ו:) מדאסר רחמנא חלב של פסולי המוקדשין, ולא קאמר דאיצטריך משום ההוא דלאחר שחיטה! ומיהו מצינו למימר דאיצטריך קרא "תשפכנו כמים" משום דם שיצא קודם שחיטת רוב. אבל מ״מ קשה מהא דשמעתין. ואומר רבי: דס״ד למיסר כמו (חלב והוו בשר), וה״ה בשר ולא דם; ולא דמי לגיזה, דשמא דגיזה מ"תזבח" נפקא, דמשמע: תזבח ולא תגוז. אבל כאן "ואכלת בשר" כתיב (דברים י״ב:ט״ו) — משמע: בשר תאכל, ולא חלב ודם, ולאסור אפי' בהנאה; אע״פ שהדרשה אינה מיושבת על הדם כמו חלב, דשרי באכילה הוא. והא דלא מייתי התם "בשר ולא חלב", אלא "תזבח ולא גיזה" — ריש מילתא נקט. ועוד: ניחא ליה לאתויי איסור גיזה אפי' לענין מלקו', כמו מתחלה קודם שנפלו, (דתנן): "הגוזז והעובד סופג ארבעים"; וכיון שהחמירה בו תורה כל כך, ה״א לדרוש קראי לחומרא: "בשר" — ולא חלב ודם, אי לאו "כמים". וכן מוכח בפרק קמא (לעיל בכורות ו:): דהא דדרשינן "בשר ולא חלב", לא שיהא אסור לחלוב — דבעו למידק מינה היתר חלב, מדגלי רחמנא גבי פסולי המוקדשין "בשר ולא חלב", הא דחולין שרי; שמע מינה דלאסור החלב שנחלב אתא קרא:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:17:1.english: "The hair of a blemished firstborn that shed, etc." - This entire sugya proves that [deriving benefit from] the fleece of disqualified consecrated animals is permitted by Torah law. And even as for the Rabbis who forbid [it], the Gemara explains [that this is] a decree: lest one come to postpone [the animal's slaughter]. And that which we expound above (Bekhorot 6b): "You may slaughter" — and not shearing, this means: "You may slaughter" — and you may not shear [i.e., perform the act of shearing]. And this is puzzling to the Rebbe: For we say in the second chapter of Chullin (35b–36a) regarding [the verse] "Upon the earth you shall pour it out like water" (Deuteronomy 12:16): That [verse] comes to permit [benefit from] the blood of disqualified consecrated animals; for it might have entered your mind to say: Since they are forbidden in shearing and labor, their blood should also require burial; [therefore, the verse] teaches us [that it is permitted for benefit]. And how could it enter our mind to forbid their blood [from benefit] because they are forbidden in shearing and labor? Behold, even the fleece itself is permitted [from benefit by Torah law]! And if you say: That which is permitted by Torah law is [only wool that] shed [naturally], but [actively] shearing, where one intends [to shear], is forbidden — [this cannot be, for] first: intentional [drawing] of blood is like naturally shed fleece [since slaughtering is a permissible and commanded act, not an illicit harvesting]! And furthermore: they disagree even regarding one who plucks [wool intentionally], as is proven at the end of our chapter (Bekhorot 26a), where [Akavya] permits [it], which implies that when the Rabbis forbid [it], it is only rabbinically. And even with regard to an unblemished burnt offering, the fleece is not forbidden except rabbinically [after slaughter], as is proven below regarding one who plucks wool from an unblemished burnt offering; and that which [the Gemara there] challenges: "One who plucks — is there anyone who permits it?!" — that is rabbinically, as explained there in the Kunteres [Rashi], because he is a wicked person [who intentionally transgressed, and the Rabbis penalized him]. And furthermore, there is a difficulty with that [passage] in Chullin: Why do I need a verse [to teach that] the blood of disqualified consecrated animals is permitted for benefit? For even with [valid] consecrated offerings, blood is permitted for benefit once its mitzvah has been performed [i.e., sprinkled on the altar]; and there [in disqualified offerings], where there is no mitzvah [to sprinkle], why should it be forbidden?! And furthermore: What is meant by [the Gemara in Chullin saying]: "Since they are forbidden in shearing and labor"? But after slaughter it is permitted to shear and to work, as from slaughter onward everything is permitted — and there [in Chullin], it is dealing with the blood of slaughter! And milk as well, we do not forbid [from benefit by Torah law] from that which is written "meat" [except] during its life, but not after slaughter — just as according to the one who expounds above in the second chapter (Bekhorot 15b): "You have permission to eat of them only from the time of slaughter onward." And furthermore: it is permitted according to everyone, since [the Gemara] sought to derive the permissibility of milk in the first chapter (above, Bekhorot 6b) from the fact that the Merciful One forbade the milk of disqualified consecrated animals, and it did not say that [the verse] was needed on account of that [milk] which is after slaughter! However, we could say that the verse "you shall pour it out like water" was needed on account of blood that emerged prior to the slaughter of the majority [of the neck organs]. But nevertheless, the difficulty from our sugya remains. And the Rebbe says: It could have entered our mind to forbid [the blood] like [milk, and the verse would mean: "meat," but not blood]. And it is not similar to shearing: for shearing is perhaps derived from "you may slaughter," which implies: you may slaughter, but not shear [meaning an active prohibition against shearing]. But here, "and you shall eat meat" is written (Deuteronomy 12:15), which implies: meat you may eat, but not milk or blood, and to forbid them even from benefit — even though the derivation does not sit as smoothly upon blood as it does upon milk, which is [normally] permitted for consumption [whereas non-sacred blood is already forbidden to eat, so "meat and not blood" must forbid benefit]. And that which [the Gemara] there does not cite "meat and not milk," but rather "you may slaughter and not shear" — it cited the beginning of the matter [the first clause of the verse]. And furthermore: it was preferable for it to cite the prohibition of shearing, [to show that sanctity remains] even regarding lashes just as originally before they fell [i.e., became blemished], as we learned in a Mishna: "One who shears or works [with a consecrated animal] incurs forty [lashes]"; and since the Torah was so stringent regarding it, it would have entered our mind to expound the verses stringently: "meat" — but not milk or blood, were it not for [the verse] "like water." And so it is proven in the first chapter (above, Bekhorot 6b): for that which we expound "meat and not milk" does not mean that it is forbidden to milk [the animal], for they sought to deduce from it the permissibility of [all] milk, since the Merciful One revealed with regard to disqualified consecrated animals: "meat and not milk" — which implies that that of non-sacred animals is permitted; deduce from this that the verse comes to forbid the milk that was milked:

Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:2:1.hebrew: מסוכריא דנזייתא - פירשנו בפ"ק דכתובות (ד' ו. ד"ה האי), ובסוף (כל כתבי) (שבת קיא. ד"ה האי):
Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:2:1.english: The stopper of a barrel - We explained [this] in the first chapter of Ketubot (6a, s.v. Hai) and at the end of [the chapter entitled] Kol Kitvei (Shabbat 111a, s.v. Hai).

Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:5:1.hebrew: דהוה ליה עוקר דבר מגידולו כלאחר יד - אין ללמוד מכאן שיהא מותר לתלוש נוצה מצואר של עוף כדי לשחוט בי"ט, דהא לעיל פריש דהא דשרי הכא משום שאין מתכוין. וללשון נמי שפירש דאפי' במתכוין — בנוצה לא הוי כלאחר יד, כדקתני בסמוך בתולש את העוף. ואע"ג דאין צריך כאן נוצה והוי מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, אין ללמוד מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה מכלאחר יד:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:5:1.english: Because it is uprooting an item from its place of growth in an unusual manner - One cannot infer from here that it should be permitted to pluck a feather from the neck of a bird in order to slaughter [it] on a Festival. For above it was explained that that which is permitted here is because it is unintentional; and also according to the explanation that [it is permitted] even when intentional, in the case of a feather it is not [considered done] in an unusual manner, as is taught nearby regarding "one who plucks a bird." And even though one has no need for the feather here, so it is a labor not needed for its own sake, one cannot derive [that] a labor not needed for its own sake [is permitted] from [an action performed] in an unusual manner.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:6:1.hebrew: ואמר ר"ל חייב משום גוזז - תימה: מה הוא מקשה? אע"ג דלענין בכור לא מחייב ביה משום לא תגוז, לענין שבת יש לחייב משום תולדה דגוזז, ככל עוקר דבר מגידולו בבעלי חיים; כמו חולין (דף עג.): הושיט ידו למעי בהמה ודילדל עובר שבמעיה — לענין שבת [חייב], ובמוקדשין לא מחייב משום גוזז. וכן קיטוף חייב בשבת משום תולדה דקוצר, וכן תולש מן המחובר — אע"ג דקיטוף לענין קצירה קודם לעומר לא מחייב (פסחים יא.), ולענין לקט בפ' ראשית הגז (חולין קלז.). ואי הוה מפרשינן הכא דפריך אהא דאמרינן דתולש חשוב כלאחר יד — הוה ניחא, דמייתי ראיה מהכא דלא כלאחר יד; ואין הלשון משמע כן, מדקאמר "ותולש לאו היינו גוזז והא תניא התולש את העוף כו'", משמע דפריך אהא דאמרן דתולש לאו היינו גוזז:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:6:1.english: "And Reish Lakish says: Liable due to shearing" - It is astonishing: What is [the Gemara's] difficulty? Even though regarding a firstborn one is not liable for it under [the negative commandment of] "you shall not shear," regarding Shabbat one should be liable as a derivative labor of shearing, like anyone who uproots something from its place of growth in living creatures! Just as [in] Chullin (73a): [If] one reached his hand into an animal's womb and detached a fetus in its womb — regarding Shabbat [he is liable], but regarding consecrated animals he is not liable for shearing. And similarly, picking [by hand] is liable on Shabbat as a derivative labor of reaping, and likewise plucking from that which is attached [to the ground] — even though picking [by hand] regarding reaping prior to the omer does not incur liability (Pesachim 11a), nor regarding gleanings in the chapter [entitled] Reishit HaGez (Chullin 137a). And if we were to explain here that [the Gemara] is objecting to that which we said, that plucking is considered [done] in an unconventional manner, it would be fine, since it would be bringing a proof from here that it is not [done] in an unconventional manner; yet the wording does not imply this, since it says: "And is plucking not shearing? But isn't it taught: One who plucks the bird, etc.," which implies that it is objecting to that which we said, that plucking is not shearing.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:7:1.hebrew: מדרב סבר לה כר' יוסי בן המשולם ר' יוסי סבר לה כרב - דאמר: דבר שאין מתכוין אסור — שאם היה סובר דדבר שאין מתכוין מותר, מנא ליה לרב שיהא הלכה כמותו משום דתולש לאו היינו כגוזז? דילמא כי שרי ר' יוסי משום דבר שאין מתכוין מותר, ותולש היינו גוזז! אלא קים ליה לרב (משום) דאית ליה לר' יוסי: דבר שאין מתכוין אסור:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:7:1.english: “From [the fact] that Rav holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam, Rabbi Yosei holds in accordance with Rav” - For [Rav] says [that] an unintentional act is prohibited — for if [Rabbi Yosei] held that an unintentional act is permitted, from where would Rav know that the halakhah is in accordance with him because plucking is not [the same as] shearing? Perhaps when Rabbi Yosei permits [it, it is] because an unintentional act is permitted, whereas plucking is [indeed the same as] shearing! Rather, it is clear to Rav (because) that Rabbi Yosei holds [that] an unintentional act is prohibited.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:8:1.hebrew: עיקרן משחיר וראשן מאדים - כך היה כתוב בספרים. ויש לפרש דנקט "ראשן מאדים" לרבותא: אע"ג שכולה אדומה מבחוץ — טעונה גזיזה. ובקונט' גריס איפכא, מתוך תוספתא דפרה:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:8:1.english: "Their roots are black and their tips are red" - So it was written in the books [of the Gemara]. And it can be explained that [the baraita] formulated "their tips are red" as a novelty: even though [the heifer] is entirely red from the outside, it [still] requires shearing. And in the Kunteres [Rashi], he reads the opposite, based on the Tosefta of Parah.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:8:2.hebrew: גוזז במספרים ואינו חושש - כלומר: אפי' יגזוז משאר השערות בלא מתכוין, אף אלו עצמו יגזוז יותר מן הצורך לגירסת הקונט' "ראשן משחיר", והיה מדקדק דקסבר: דבר שאין מתכוין מותר. ובקונט' פי' דדייק מהא דשרי משום דאין מתכוין לשום גזיזה אלא לתקן — דאין זה כשאר לשון "אין מתכוין" בעלמא, דכיון דבכוונה גוזז במספרים. ויש ליישב לפי' הקונטרס, דהכי פריך: וסבר ר' יוסי בן המשולם דבר שאין מתכוין אסור, ושרי מטעם דתולש לאו היינו גוזז? הא אשכחן גבי פרה, דאפי' במספרים דהוי גוזז, משום דעושה כדי להכשיר הפרה — שרי; גבי בכור נמי, הוה ליה למישרי בכל ענין, כיון דעושה לצורך תיקון שחיטה, דאין זה חשוב גוזז! ומיהו אין פי' זה נראה כלל, דבכל ענין יכול להקשות: בין הוי טעמיה משום דבר שאין מתכוין מותר, בין הוי טעמיה משום דתולש לאו היינו גוזז:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 25a:8:2.english: "One shears with scissors and need not be concerned" - That is to say: Even if he unintentionally shears some of the other hairs, or even [if] he shears more than necessary of these [hairs] themselves according to the reading of the Kuntres [which reads] "their tops are black," [he need not be concerned;] and [the Gemara] inferred from this that he holds that an unintentional act is permitted. And in the Kuntres, it was explained that [the Gemara] inferred this from the fact that it is permitted because he does not intend for any shearing, but rather to rectify [the animal] — though this is not like the usual sense of "unintentional" elsewhere, since he intentionally shears with scissors. And one could resolve [the text] according to the explanation of the Kuntres, that this is what [the Gemara] is asking: Does Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam really hold that an unintentional act is prohibited, and [in the case of a firstborn] it is permitted [only] because plucking is not [considered] shearing? But we find regarding the heifer that even with scissors, which is [actual] shearing, it is permitted because he does it in order to render the heifer fit; regarding a firstborn as well, he should have permitted it in any manner, since he does it for the purpose of preparing for slaughter, as this is not considered shearing! However, this explanation does not appear [correct] at all, for in any case [the Gemara] could object: whether his reason is that an unintentional act is permitted, or whether his reason is that plucking is not [considered] shearing.
